purpose: Backfill explicit modern source-governance fields for six high-dependency P1 canonical sources while holding Brazil TSE outside the tranche until its provenance scope is repaired.

china_nbs.finding: NBS expressly permits download and use of statistical data and reasonable attributed quotation/reprint, but does not expressly grant crawler or scraper access.

india_mospi.finding: MoSPI GSDD 2026 treats Category A aggregated/analyzed information and publications as open-access without registration, including commercial use; website automation remains a separate endpoint question.

us_eia.finding: EIA U.S. Government publications are public domain subject to third-party exceptions; schedule-page polling remains an endpoint/operational review matter.

fao.finding: FAO distinguishes general website content from separately licensed publications and statistical databases. The release-calendar HTML is governed conservatively as general web content unless a separately reviewed route applies.

who.finding: WHO general website terms support research/private-study excerpts but require authorization for substantial or other uses; no production automation grant is inferred for governance-calendar pages or user-facing calendar exports.

unfccc.finding: UNFCCC official texts, data and documents are public domain with acknowledgement, but that scope is not projected onto arbitrary automated polling of the COP event webpage.

brazil_tse_amendment.finding: Resolution 23.771 of 3 August 2026 amends the 2026 electoral calendar in Resolution 23.760.

brazil_constitution.finding: Constitution art. 82, as amended by EC 111/2021, provides that the presidential term begins on 5 January of the year following the election; this is the proper basis for the 2027 inauguration/start-date fact.

set.governance_backfill_basis: NBS permits use of statistical data and attributed factual content, but its terms do not expressly clear crawler/scraper access to the release-calendar surface.
MoSPI Category A statistical publications are open-access, while website automation remains separately unresolved and the dynamic calendar is currently inconsistent with the authoritative ARC PDF.
EIA factual/public-domain content supports curated provenance; existing read-only WPSR pilot use does not itself clear unrestricted schedule-page polling.
FAO general website terms support attributed non-commercial informational use; the separate statistical-database licensing regime is not projected onto the release-calendar HTML endpoint.
WHO general website terms support limited research/private-study use but do not clear production automation; user-facing calendar export transport is not treated as permission.
UNFCCC official schedule facts remain authoritative, but the public-domain status of official texts/data/documents is not projected into a production automation licence for the COP event webpage.

WSSRC-EL-BR-001.reason: The TSE electoral-calendar source correctly supports election-cycle milestones but is not the proper provenance basis for the constitutionally grounded 5 January 2027 presidential inauguration/start date. Governance backfill is held until that source relationship is repaired.
